changes.after: An air traffic controller issued a take-off clearance to the Flight 386 for runway 30R. At the same time, an airport operations officer was operating a vehicle on that runway. The controller had previously issued a clearance to the operations officer to conduct bird dispersal activities on the runway. The operations officer was monitoring his radio and heard Flight 386's take-off clearance. He told the controller that he would vacate the runway. At the same time, the flight crew had observed the vehicle on the runway and did not commence the takeoff. The controller cancelled the take-off clearance until the runway was clear. The investigation found that the controller didn't keep eyes on the runway because he was concentrating on heavy traffic. Another possible reason was that the controller was experiencing some degree of fatigue at the time.

changes.after: The incident occurred on 22 October 2005. An Airbus 319 was operating a scheduled passenger flight from London to Paris. As the aircraft climbed to FL 200 at night, there was a major electrical failure. This resulted in the loss of some important aircraft systems. Thecrew reported that both the captains and co-pilots PFDs and NDs didnt work, nor did the upper ECAM display. The autopilot andautothrust systems disconnected, the VHF radio and intercom were inoperative and most of the cockpit lighting went off. The captain maintained control of the aircraft with standby instruments. The co-pilot carried out the abnormal checklist actions which appeared on the lower ECAM display, the only available electronic flight display in the aircraft. Most of the affected systems were restored after about 90 seconds, when the co-pilot selected the Ac Essential Feed switch to Alternate. There were no injuries to any of the 76 passengers or 6 crew.

changes.after: On August 14, 2005 at approximately 12:00 p.m local Greek time, a Boeing 737-300, crashed into rolling terrain northeast of Athens, Greece. Greek authorities suggested the failure of pressurization in the aircraft may have caused the crash when they ruled out a terrorist attack.

changes.after: On 18 January 2005, a Beech aircraft sustained damage when its main landing gear collapsed during touchdown on runway 24 at Perth Airport, WA. The aircraft had earlier departed the aerodrome on a charter flight with one pilot and seven passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, the pilot selected the landing gear up and subsequently observed that the red gear-in-transit warning light remained illuminated. An aerodrome controller noticed that the aircrafts landing gear did not retract and passed that information to the departures controller. The departures controller cleared the pilot to climb to 4, 000 ft and provided radar vectors to a suitable area where the pilot could complete troubleshooting of the aircraft systems. The pilot completed the checklist actions in an attempt to manually extend the landing gear. However, the green gear down indicator lights did not illuminate The pilot returned to Perth Airport and conducted a fly-past of the aerodrome control tower and maintenance facility at an altitude of about 500 ft. Engineer and air traffic control witnesses to that flypast indicated to the pilot that the landing gear appeared to be in the extended position. During the subsequent landing, the right main landing gear collapsed and retracted into the wheel well. The left main landing gear partially retracted into the wheel well and the nose gear remained extended. The right engine nacelle fuel tank was punctured, requiring removal of the remaining fuel in that tank prior to the aircrafts removal from the runway.

changes.after: A witness reported that he observed the aircraft taxi to the eastern end of the runway and commence the take-off roll but lost sight of the aircraft as it moved along the runway. The pilot stated that the take-off roll was from a rolling start with power being slowly applied until engine output stabilized. At about 90 kts indicated air speed, the pilot attempted to rotate the aircraft but encountered resistance to rearward movement of the control column. He decided to reject the takeoff because the aircraft speed at the time was below his nominated decision speed of 100 kts. The pilot reported that he then reduced the engine power to idle and applied maximum braking. The aircraft overran the runway, passed through the airport boundary fence, continued across a public road, and passed through another fence before coming to a stop 162 mbeyond the end of the runway. An inspection of the runway revealed a skid mark from the aircrafts right tire, which commenced 65 m before the end of the runway. After the aircraft came to a stop, the pilot exited the aircraft via the crew door, assisted the passengers to evacuate the aircraft through the rear cabin door and marshalled them to an area away from the aircraft. A passenger then used a mobile phone to contact emergency services, who attended the scene soon after.

changes.after: A Boeing 737-200 was scheduled to operate a regular public transport flight from Hobartto Sydney on 17 May 2005 departing at 0600 Eastern Standard Time with 6 crew members and 26 passengers. During the starting of the right engine, the aircraft dispatcher informed the flight crew that there was smoke and sparks shooting from the right engine and advised to get everyone off. The pilot in command called for an emergency evacuation without initiating the Passenger Evacuation Checklist. As a result, the wing flaps were not set to the extended position and the tail section of the aircraft was dark without emergency lighting while passengers were exiting the aircraft. The forward Door Right 1 escape slide fell to the ground un-inflated when the door was opened. A number of ground personnel ran to the front of the aircraft and helped 22 passengers off the forward Door Left 1 slide and directed them towards the terminal. Fourpassengers exited by the Door 2 slide at the rear of the aircraft and ran into the middle of the apron. The over-wing exits were not opened. The aircrafts dispatcher had not received any education in emergency communications with flight crew nor aircraft evacuations at the terminal. The reported smoke and sparks was a result of the right engine air turbine starter failing during the engine start sequence.

changes.after: The DC-10 aircraft was flying from Kingstonto Toronto Airport. The aircraft departed Kingston at 1400 Eastern Standard Time with the first office designated as the pilot flying. During the initial climb following take-off, the first officer noted that abnormal forward pressure on the control column was required to keep the aircraft from pitching nose up. Tocounter the pitch-up, he trimmed the aircraft nose down. Thirty seconds after becoming airborne, the aircraft was 350 feet above ground level and the first officer had applied full nose-down trim. The amount of forward pressure on the control column continued to increase as the aircraft accelerated, and the first officer notified the captain of the control difficulties and requested his assistance in holding the control column forward. As the aircraft climbed, the captain declared an emergency, indicating that they were experiencing control difficulties and that the aircraft may have to land nearby. The flight crew leveled the aircraft at 4000 feet on the sea level and pulled the elevator pitch disconnect handle, isolating the left and right elevators. The captain's elevator control functioned normally after the disconnection, and he decided to continue the flight. The flight crew conducted a flapless landing at Toronto without further incident. When the aircraft was inspected after landing, the right-side elevator spring tab was jammed in the trailing-edge-down position.

这架DC-10型飞机当时正从金斯敦飞往多伦多机场。飞机于东部标准时间14点从金斯敦起飞，由副驾驶担任操纵飞行员。

在起飞后的初始爬升阶段，副驾驶注意到需要在操纵杆上施加异常的向前推力，才能防止飞机机头上扬。为了抵消机头的上仰，他将飞机的配平调整为机头向下。飞机起飞30秒后，高度达到了离地面350英尺，此时副驾驶已经将配平调至最大的机头向下位置。随着飞机加速，需要在操纵杆上施加的向前推力继续增大，副驾驶告知机长飞机操纵出现困难，并请求机长帮忙向前按住操纵杆。

changes.after: On May 25, 2002, a Boeing 747-200 aircraft performed the flight from Taiwan Chung Cheng airport to Hongkong international airport, carrying 206 passengers and 19 crew members on board. It broke up and crashed at an altitude of 34, 900 feet 23 miles northeast of Magong City in Penghu County, killing all those on board. It is the deadliest air disaster in Taiwan. After careful investigation, scientists found the full story of the crash. About 20 years ago, the plane landed heavily at Kai Tak Airport in Hong Kong and damaged the skin on its tail. After the damage to the tail, China Airlines only covered the area with a piece of aluminum plate similar to the damaged skin and painted it. Instead of replacing the whole skin in accordance with the maintenance guidelines issued by Boeing. This cause a buildup of metal fatigue in the area. For 22 years, maintenance crews had not noticed anythirng unusual. After the split, the aircraft experienced decompression disintegration. According to the fuselage recovered after the accident, the crack is at least 90.5 inches long, and studies have shown that the structure could collapse if the crack is more than 58 inches in the air.

changes.after: Jiuzhai Huanglong Airport, also known as Jiuzhaigou Airport and Jiuhuang Airport, is an airport in Songpan County, Sichuan province. It is about 240 km from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport, an important aviation hub of Southwest China. It is one of the highest airport in the world with an altitude of3448 meters. So it is considered one of the most difficult airports to fly to in China, aircraft must typically fly at afaster airspeed in order to takeoff or land, but those who fly over here are also amazed by the beautiful scenery. Due to the high elevation, some passengers may experience symotomsof altitude sickness. This should be taken into consideration when planning to fly into or out of the airport.

changes.after: On April 29th 2013, a National Air Cargo Boeing 747-400 freighter on behalf of US Mobility Command, performing cargo flight from Bagram to Dubai with 7 crew and cargo consisting of 5 military vehicles, has crashed shortly after takeoff. 2013年4月29日，一架代表美国机动司令部的美国国家航空货运公司（National Air Cargo）的波音747-400型货机，搭载着7名机组人员和包括5辆军用车辆在内的货物，执行从巴格拉姆飞往迪拜的货运航班任务，在起飞后不久坠毁。据报道，机上7名机组人员全部在此次坠机事故中遇难。

changes.after: On June 10th 2018, an American Airlines Boeing 777-200 performing flight AA60 from Tokyo to Dallas with 269 people on board, was on approach to Dallas descending through about 9000 feet when the aircraft encountered moderate turbulence. According to National Transportation Safety Board, as the flight began its descent into KDF, the captain illuminated the seat belt sign and made a public address announcement reminding passengers to buckle up for the remainder of the flight. Then the airplane entered a band of small cumulus clouds and experienced 10-15 seconds of moderate turbulence. When the turbulence was encountered, the flight attendants were conducting their final cabin safety checks, so 7 flight attendants received minor injuries, one passenger, who ignored the seat-belt sign and instructions to remain seated, injured his left ankle. The aircraft continued for a landing on Dallas airport runway 18R without further incident about 12 minutes later. The flight crew requested parameedics to meet the airplane at the gate. Finally, the passenger was transported to the hospital, and the 7 flight attendants were treated at the airplane and released.

changes.after: On January 29th 2015, a Ryanair Boeing 737-800, performing FR-8592 from London to Bergerac, was on NDB approach Y to Bergerac's runway 28 in instrument meteorological conditions. The aircraft descended below minimum safe altitude when it was handed off to tower. The approach controller received a Minimum Safe Altitude Warning and thee aircraft's EGPWS issued a warning, too. The crew initiated a go-around and the aircraft climbed to safe altitude. Thenthe crew positioned for another approach and landed safely on runway 28 about 24 minutes after aborting the first aproach. According to the investigation, the incident occurred while the aircraft performed an NDB approach without DME, probably without external visual references. Meanwhile, the first preparation of the approach was probably incomplete or imprecise. As a result, the late modification did not permit the crew to agree on the guidance modes. This resulted in confusion of the captain as to the horizontal trajectory to be followed by the aircraft. This state of confusion led him to request an early descent below the safety altitude.

changes.before:
2015年1月29日，一架瑞安航空的波音737-800型飞机执行从伦敦飞往贝杰拉克的FR-8592航班，在仪表气象条件下，采用无方向信标（NDB）进近方式，朝着贝杰拉克机场28号跑道进近。

当飞机移交给塔台管制时，它下降到了最低安全高度以下。进近管制员收到了最低安全高度警告，飞机的增强型近地警告系统（EGPWS）也发出了警告。机组人员启动了复飞程序，飞机爬升至安全高度。然后机组人员重新调整位置准备再次进近，并在放弃第一次进近约24分钟后，安全降落在28号跑道上。

根据调查，这起事件发生在飞机在没有测距仪（DME）且可能没有外部目视参考的情况下进行无方向信标进近时。同时，第一次进近的准备工作可能不完整或不准确。因此，后期的修正没能让机组人员就引导模式达成一致。这导致机长对于飞机应遵循的水平航线感到困惑。这种困惑的状态使他要求飞机提前下降到安全高度以下。

changes.after: On October 25th 2018, a Vueling Airbus A320-200, performing flight VY-1431 from Bilbao to Barcelona with 114 passengers and 6 crew, departed Bilbao's runway. At that time, the left engine dropped two bonnets. In the absence of any abnormal indicationss and unaware of the separation, the crew continued the flight to Barcelona for a safe landing. Although a part of the engine cowling became stuck in the left main gear, the gear retracted normally after takeoff and extended in Barcelona without prololems. The aircraft received minor damage at the left main gear and the left side of the fuselage where debris hit, however all persons on board disembarked normally, no medical attention was needed. Theinvestigation has determined that the incident was caused by flying the airplane without closing and properly latching the cowls on the airplane's left engine, which was in turn caused by an improper maintenance operation, and by the incorrect performance of the walk-around check prior to the flight.

changes.after: On Nov 20th 2013, an Atlas Air Boeing 747-400 Drealmlifter, performing freight flight 5Y4241 from New York to Wichita McConnell Airbase, with 2 crew, was on a GPS/RNAV approach to McConnel Airport's runway 19L, but unintentionally landed on runway 18 of Wichita's Jabara Airport, and managed to stop the aircraft on the runway. McConnell Tower then reported the coordinates of Beech Airport, the crew returned the coordinates, after which tower identified the airport as Jabara according to those position data. In the meantime a person on the ground had arrived at the aircraft and told the crew the local frequency. The aircraft and airport sustained no damage.

changes.after: A bmi Regional Embraer ERJ-145, performing flight BM1753 from Munich to Norrkoping with18 passegers and 3 crew, was self-positioning for an ILS approach to Norrkoping's runway 27. The aircraft was cleared to descend to 2100 feet and cleared the approach to runway27. At the same time an ultralight aircraft was operating below the controlled airspace in uncontrolled airspace performing a VFR flight, the two aircraft were on different radio frequencies. While still positioning to intercept the localizer, the aircraft automatically turned west and began to descend, one pilot believed they were capturing the glideslope, the other pilot believed they were on localizer and above glide. The crew changed from automatic glideslope coupling to vertical speed and increased the rate of descent to re-capture theglideslope. The crew subsequently queried about the target on their TCAS screen and the altitude of the Embraer. When the distance reduced to 1 nautical mile horizontally and 200 feet vertically, the Embraer's TCAS issued a resolution advisory, and the crew initiated ago around. The aircraft positioned for another approach and landed safely about 10 minutes later.

changes.after: A Delta Airlines Airbus 330, performing a flight from New York to Paris, was en route atFL380 about 700 nm southwest of Reykjavik airport, Iceland when the crew decided to divert to Iceland, reporting with left hand engine failure. The crew requested to descend to FL320 and set course for Reykjavik. The diversion was approved by Oceanic Control within a minute, however, the request to descent took more than 15 minutes due to a lot of traffic around that needed to be moved out. The aircraft continued to maintain FL380 in the meantime. Finally, the aircraft descended to FL290 and landed safely on Iceland about 2 hours after the decision to divert. After the landing, another aircraft was sent from Amsterdam to fly the 96 passengers and cargo from lceland to Paris. According to the investigation, the crew attempte to move the thrust lever back and forth when the engine started to vibrate, but this resulted in the ergine stalling a number of times. Thecrew thus declared emergency and diverted to Iceland on single engine.

changes.after: A visual approach is an ATC authorization foraircrafit on IFR flight plan to proceed visually to the airport, even to the landing. It is not an instrument approach procedure, and there is no missed approach segment. Even when an aircraft is being vectored for an instrument approach, controllers may initiate or pilots may request a visual approach provided the pilot subsequently reports the airport or runway in sight. Before clearing an aircraft for a visual approach, controllers should ensure that weather conditions at the airport are VFR, and they need resolve potential conflicts with all other aircraft. The pilot must, at all times, have either the airport or the preceding aircraft in sight. This approach must be authorized and under the control of the appropriate air traffic control facility. Reported weather at the airport must be ceiling at or above 1000 ft, and visibility of 3 miles or greater. An aircraft unable to complete visual approach shall be handled as any "go around", and appropriate separation must be provided.

changes.before:
目视进近是空中交通管制（ATC）对处于仪表飞行规则（IFR）飞行计划中的飞机的一种许可，允许其以目视方式飞往机场，甚至直接着陆。它并非一种仪表进近程序，且不存在复飞航段。

即使一架飞机正按引导进行仪表进近，只要飞行员随后报告已看到机场或跑道，管制员也可以发起、或者飞行员可以请求进行目视进近。在批准一架飞机进行目视进近之前，管制员应确保机场的天气状况符合目视飞行规则（VFR），并且他们需要解决与所有其他飞机之间可能存在的冲突。

飞行员在任何时候都必须能够看到机场或前方的飞机。这种进近方式必须得到相应空中交通管制机构的批准并处于其管控之下。机场所报告的天气状况必须是：云底高度达到或高于1000英尺，能见度为3英里或更远。

一架无法完成目视进近的飞机应按照任何“复飞”情况来处理，并且必须为其提供适当的间隔。

changes.before: When SIA188 was approaching the airspace of Chicago Area Control Center, the controller instructed the flight crew to change radio frequency for the next sector on 132.1. The first officer acknowledged the frequency change and read back the correct frequency. However, the flight crew did not contact ATC on the new frequency. Because the controllers in the receiving units were preparing for a shift change, they didn’t know that flight 188 did not establish radio contact, 30 minutes later, the controller at the next sector identified SIA188 on the radar. Although they attempted to establish contact with the airplane by calling the company dispatcher, they got no response from the pilots. The controller finally regained contact with SIA188 on the emergency frequency 50 minutes later.

changes.before: Landing light signal could provide useful information to controllers. One day, a B757 vacated runway 36L via taxiway A9 after landing. It was then cleared to cross runway 36R. But it stopped taxiing on taxiway A9 between runway 36L and runway 36R. The tower controller attempted to contact the pilot but received no reply. He saw the aircraft landing lights were also off. This made him believe that the B757 had a radio failure and had not received the clearance to cross runway 36R. So he issued takeoff clearance to A320 on runway 36R. Suddenly, the controller noticed the B757’s lights came on and it began to move. Realizing the risk of runway incursion, he cancelled A320’s takeoff clearance immediately.

changes.before: One day, Flight 123, a B737 carrying 152 passengers and 9 crews was flying to land at Tokyo International Airport. When it was transferred from Tokyo Control to Tokyo Approach, flight 123 was instructed to proceed to DA to hold because of traffic congestion. During the holding, the flight crew was informed that the local weather was deteriorating and the controller suggested the pilot divert to the alternate, but the pilot reported that their fuel was not enough to the alternate. So the controller vectored flight 123 by radar to land at runway 34R. Unfortunately, the pilot couldn’t stabilize the aircraft on the localizer due to wind shear. Flight 123 went around and made a second approach. Later, it crashed into a hillside due to fuel shortage. The aircraft was broken into pieces and all the people on board were killed.

Three minutes later, Indonesia 205 passed the outer marker inbound. At that time, the controller issued a missed approach clearance because of separation. He instructed Indonesia 205 to make a right turn to a heading of 180 and climb to 900m. But during the missed approach, the aircraft was out of control because of mechanical problem. The aircraft continued to descend with a high angle of attack. The aircraft impacted trees and buildings and part of the fuselage was damaged.

changes.before: One day, AFR188 crashed at Singapore Changi Airport during takeoff. The tower controller instructed the crew to takeoff on Runway 02L, but the crew lined up runway 02R and began their takeoff rolling. The aircraft overran the runway, and crashed into the fence of the airport. Crew members and 110 passengers were killed, and the co-pilot was badly injured. The plane was destroyed by the impact and caught on an intense fire. According to the investigation, there were three reasons leading to the accidents. First of all, the crew didn’t use effective methods to verify their position at the airport. Secondly, the crew forgot to check whether they were on the correct runway or not. Finally, the crew members’ idle chatting during the taxi resulted the loss of situational awareness.

changes.before: CSN341 was a flight from Beijing to Los Angles. When CSN341 initially contacted the tower controller, he was told the runway visual range was 500m. The pilot executed a missed approach two minutes later because of no contact at minima. Then, CSN341 was given radar vectors for a second ILS approach. In the second approach, the controller issued landing clear to CSN341 at outer marker. One minute later, the controller observed the airplane was leaving the glide path on his radar display, so he issued missed approach instructions again. There was no further reply from the pilot. The airplane impacted the top of a tall building and crashed. According to the investigation, the poor visibility made the pilot nervous and he misunderstood the missed approach instructions and made a wrong turn.

Through good communication, the controller understood the flight crew wanted to return to land. But the pilot had to dump fuel before landing because the aircraft was overweight to land. changes.before:
On September 28, 2003, United 552, a DC-9-82, experienced an in-flight engine fire during departure climb from New York City. During the return to the departure airport, the nose landing gear failed to extend, and the flight crew was instructed by the ATC to execute a go-around, during which the crew extended the nose gear using the emergency procedure. The flight crew conducted an emergency landing, and the 2 flight crewmembers, 3 flight attendants, and 138 passengers deplaned on the runway. No occupant injuries were reported, but the airplane sustained substantial damage from the fire.
The National Transportation Safety Board determines that the probable cause of this accident was American Airlines’ maintenance personnel’s use of an inappropriate manual engine-start procedure, which led to the subsequent left engine fire. (128 words)

The incident occurred on 22 October 2005. An Airbus 319 was operating a scheduled passenger flight from London to Paris. As the aircraft climbed to FL 200 at night, there was a major electrical failure. This resulted in the loss of some important aircraft systems. The crew reported that both the captain’s and co-pilot’s PFDs and NDs didn’t work, nor did the upper ECAM display. The autopilot and autothrust systems disconnected, the VHF radio and intercom were inoperative and most of the cockpit lighting went off. The captain maintained control of the aircraft with standby instruments. The co-pilot carried out the abnormal checklist actions which appeared on the lower ECAM display, the only available electronic flight display in the aircraft.
Most of the affected systems were restored after about 90 seconds, when the co-pilot selected the AC Essential Feed switch to Alternate. There were no injuries to any of the 76 passengers or 6 crew. (152words)

On July 13, 2003, Air Sunshine Airlines, a Cessna was ditched in the Atlantic Ocean following the in-flight failure of the right engine. Four of the nine passengers sustained no injuries, three passengers and the pilot sustained minor injuries, and one adult and one child passenger died after they evacuated the airplane. The airplane sustained substantial damage. The airplane was being operated as a scheduled international passenger commuter flight from F Hollywood International Airport, Florida, to MYAT. Visual meteorological conditions prevailed for the flight, which operated on a visual flight rules flight plan.
The National Transportation Safety Board determines that the probable cause of this accident was the in-flight failure of the right engine and the pilot’s failure to adequately manage the airplane’s performance after the engine failed. The right engine failure resulted from inadequate maintenance that was performed by Air Sunshine’s maintenance personnel.

On March 23 1994 the aircraft named Glinka, after the father of Russian music, was flying from Moscow to Hong Kong. There were sixty-three passengers with twelve crew members on board.
The aircraft crashed after a captain allowed his child to manipulate the controls of the plane. The pilot's 11 year old daughter and 16 year old son were taking turns in the pilot's seat. While the boy was flying, the captain inadvertently disengaged the autopilot linkage to the ailerons and put the airliner in a bank of 90 degrees which caused the nose to drop sharply.
The co-pilot pulled back on the yoke to obtain level flight but the plane stalled. With his seat pulled all the way back, the co-pilot in the right hand seat could not properly control the aircraft. After several stalls and rapid pull-ups the plane went into a spiral descent. In the end, the co-pilot initiated a pull-up and nearly regained a stable flight path but the aircraft struck the ground in an almost level attitude killing all 75 aboard.

On June 10 1990 there was a flight from Birmingham, England to Malaga, Spain, when the aircraft was flying at FL 173, a large section of windshield fell away from the aircraft. The decompression pulled the captain out from under his seatbelt. Despite trying to hold onto the yoke, the captain was sucked out into the opening. He was in an immediate danger.
A steward in the cockpit was fortunately able to grab hold of his legs. Another steward was able to strap him into the vacant seat and aid in holding onto the captain's legs. The copilot wearing full restraints made an emergency landing at Southampton.
The captain remained half way out of the aircraft for 15 minutes and suffered only frostbite and some fractures. Improper bolts used to replace the windshield two days earlier resulted in the accident.

On August 14, 2005 at approximately 12:00 p.m local Greek time, a Boeing 737-300, crashed into rolling terrain northeast of Athens, Greece. The aircraft had departed Larnaka Airport, Cyprus, two hours and 57 minutes prior to the accident.
According to the investigation, during climb-out as the aircraft passed 12,000 feet, the cabin altitude warning horn sounded. The captain then began radio communications with his company maintenance base at Larnaka. The aircraft was on autopilot at the time and followed its FMCS inserted route. It subsequently entered the missed approach holding pattern.
Two Air Force F-16 fighter aircraft intercepted the aircraft emergency call and one of the pilots noticed that the captain's seat was empty and the first officer's seat was occupied by an incapacitated person. Shortly thereafter, one person was seen to enter the cockpit wearing an oxygen mask.
After 1 hour and 12 minutes in the holding pattern the left engine flamed out due to fuel starvation and 10 minutes later the right engine also flamed out. The cabin altitude warning horn subsequently stopped sounding after the aircraft later descended below 10,000 feet during its final descent.
Greek authorities suggested the failure of pressurization in the aircraft may have caused the crash when they ruled out a terrorist attack.

The flight departed Peachtree Airport, moments later the pilot radioed that the airplane had a landing gear problem, and there was smoke in the cockpit. The pilot was instructed to enter visual traffic for Runway 2R. Once the airplane was in the traffic pattern, the controller told the pilot that it appeared that the landing gear was extended, and cleared the flight to land. As the airplane neared touchdown the controller told the pilot that the landing gear was not down and locked, and then instructed the pilot to go - around. As the pilot maneuvered the airplane for a landing on runway 27, the pilot was again instructed to go around. Seconds later the aircraft touched down in a grassy area the approach ends of runways 2R.
Examination of the airplane disclosed that the airplane had sustained extensive fire damage to the floor area beneath the pilot's seat. The examination revealed that a flex hydraulic fluid supply line was missing, and there had been electrical arcing in the immediate vicinity of the hot spot.
The National Transportation Safety Board determines the probable cause(s) of this accident as follows: The failure of the flex hydraulic line and the chaffing of an electrical line under the pilot seat that resulted in an in-flight fire.

On 18 August 2006, a Boeing 747aircraft, with a crew of 18 and 243 passengers departed Hong Kong, China, on a scheduled passenger service to Melbourne, Australia.
While in cruise, one of the cabin crew notified the flight crew that there was a smell of fuel in the first class cabin. One of the pilots verified the fuel smell and then proceeded to inspect the engines from the cabin windows.
A fluid trail was evident from the rear of the number-3 engine. During this time, it was noted by the other pilots that the number-3 engine had a higher than normal fuel flow. The flight crew conducted an in-flight shut down of the number-3 engine and diverted the aircraft to Darwin.
A subsequent inspection of the number-3 engine revealed the fuel manifold return line had fractured, causing a fuel leak. The fuel line was replaced and the aircraft was returned to service.
In 2005, the ATSB investigated two other fuel manifold return line fractures, from the same engine type, under similar circumstances.

On 18 January 2005, a Beech aircraft sustained damage when its main landing gear collapsed during touchdown on runway 24 at Perth Airport, WA.
The aircraft had earlier departed the aerodrome on a charter flight with one pilot and seven passengers on board. Shortly after takeoff, the pilot selected the landing gear up and subsequently observed that the red ‘gear-in-transit’ warning light remained illuminated. An aerodrome controller noticed that the aircraft’s landing gear did not retract and passed that information to the departures controller. The departures controller cleared the pilot to climb to 4,000 ft and provided radar vectors to a suitable area where the pilot could complete troubleshooting of the aircraft systems.
The pilot completed the checklist actions in an attempt to manually extend the landing gear. However, the green ‘gear down’ indicator lights did not illuminate
The pilot returned to Perth Airport and conducted a fly-past of the aerodrome control tower and maintenance facility at an altitude of about 500 ft. Engineer and air traffic control witnesses to that flypast indicated to the pilot that the landing gear appeared to be in the extended position.
During the subsequent landing, the right main landing gear collapsed and retracted into the wheel well. The left main landing gear partially retracted into the wheel well and the nose gear remained extended. The right engine nacelle fuel tank was punctured, requiring removal of the remaining fuel in that tank prior to the aircraft’s removal from the runway.

The Scott Aviation aircraft with two crew members and four passengers on board, took off from Montréal, Quebec, for a night instrument flight rules flight to Bromont, Quebec.
Upon approaching Bromont, the co-pilot activated the lighting system and contacted the approach. The flight crew was advised that the runway edge lights were out of order. However, the approach lights and the visual approach slope indicator did turn on.
The flight crew executed the approach, and the aircraft touched down at 300 feet to the left of Runway 05L and 1800 feet beyond the threshold. It continued on its course for a distance of approximately 1800 feet before coming to a stop in a ditch. The crew tried to stop the engines, but the left engine did not stop.
The co-pilot entered the cabin to direct the evacuation. One of the passengers tried to open the emergency exit door, but was unsuccessful. All of the aircraft's occupants exited through the main entrance door. Both pilots and one passenger sustained serious injuries, and the three remaining passengers received minor injuries. The aircraft suffered major damage.

A witness reported that he observed the aircraft taxi to the eastern end of the runway and commence the take-off roll but lost sight of the aircraft as it moved along the runway.
The pilot stated that the take-off roll was from a rolling start with power being slowly applied until engine output stabilized. At about 90 kts indicated air speed, the pilot attempted to rotate the aircraft but encountered resistance to rearward movement of the control column. He decided to reject the takeoff because the aircraft speed at the time was below his nominated decision speed of 100 kts. The pilot reported that he then reduced the engine power to idle and applied maximum braking.
The aircraft overran the runway, passed through the airport boundary fence, continued across a public road, and passed through another fence before coming to a stop 162 m beyond the end of the runway. An inspection of the runway revealed a skid mark from the aircraft’s right tire, which commenced 65 m before the end of the runway.
After the aircraft came to a stop, the pilot exited the aircraft via the crew door, assisted the passengers to evacuate the aircraft through the rear cabin door and marshalled them to an area away from the aircraft. A passenger then used a mobile phone to contact emergency services, who attended the scene soon after.

A Boeing 737-200 was scheduled to operate a regular public transport flight from Hobart to Sydney on 17 May 2005 departing at 0600 Eastern Standard Time with 6 crew members and 26 passengers.
During the starting of the right engine, the aircraft dispatcher informed the flight crew that there was smoke and sparks shooting from the right engine and advised to get everyone off. The pilot in command called for an emergency evacuation without initiating the Passenger Evacuation Checklist. As a result, the wing flaps were not set to the extended position and the tail section of the aircraft was dark without emergency lighting while passengers were exiting the aircraft. The forward Door Right 1 escape slide fell to the ground un-inflated when the door was opened. A number of ground personnel ran to the front of the aircraft and helped 22 passengers off the forward Door Left 1 slide and directed them towards the terminal. Four passengers exited by the Door 2 slide at the rear of the aircraft and ran into the middle of the apron. The over-wing exits were not opened.
The aircraft’s dispatcher had not received any education in emergency communications with flight crew nor aircraft evacuations at the terminal. The reported smoke and sparks was a result of the right engine air turbine starter failing during the engine start sequence.

The DC-10 aircraft was flying from Kingston to Toronto Airport. The aircraft departed Kingston at 1400 Eastern Standard Time with the first office designated as the pilot flying.
During the initial climb following take-off, the first officer noted that abnormal forward pressure on the control column was required to keep the aircraft from pitching nose up. To counter the pitch-up, he trimmed the aircraft nose down. Thirty seconds after becoming airborne, the aircraft was 350 feet above ground level and the first officer had applied full nose-down trim. The amount of forward pressure on the control column continued to increase as the aircraft accelerated, and the first officer notified the captain of the control difficulties and requested his assistance in holding the control column forward.
As the aircraft climbed, the captain declared an emergency, indicating that they were experiencing control difficulties and that the aircraft may have to land nearby. The flight crew leveled the aircraft at 4000 feet on the sea level and pulled the elevator pitch disconnect handle, isolating the left and right elevators. The captain's elevator control functioned normally after the disconnection, and he decided to continue the flight. The flight crew conducted a flapless landing at Toronto without further incident.
When the aircraft was inspected after landing, the right-side elevator spring tab was jammed in the trailing-edge-down position.

June 21, 2002 FAA reminds all pilots to be particularly alert in their own flight preparations as well as activities at their local airports. This week incident with the Cessna 182, which is flying into restricted airspace in Washington, D.C. clearly indicates that flight preparation is more important than ever. The C-182 was intercepted by military aircraft after inadvertently straying into the restricted airspace while attempting to avoid bad weather.
Before taking off, the pilots should contact FAA Flight Service to receive the latest information; know and understand all applicable NOTAMs, and know where the Temporary Flight Restrictions are. Also maintain high vigilance at local airports, report suspicious activities to local authorities, and take the time to secure the airplane before you leave. It is critical that pilots continue to use the highest levels of preparation, responsibility and judgment, and that they encourage others to do so as well.

Passage Eight

Passage Ten

Considering the safety of passengers, the crew requested to descend immediately and land at local airport. However, there were a lot of flights below the Boeing 737 so that it was difficult for controller to give the descent instructions initially.

Passage Eelven

 On Saturday, June 14th,1956, TWA Flight 201 departed from Los Angeles to Washington D.C. United Airlines Flight 718 left Los Angeles for Chicago. Both aircraft were initially assigned the same route,with the TWA aircraft climbing to 17000 feet and the United aircraft climbing to 21000 feet.

changes.after: On Saturday, June 14th, 1956, TWA Flight 201 departed from Los Angeles to Washington D.C. United Airlines Flight 718 left Los Angeles for Chicago. About one hour later, the pilots of both aircraft requested that they intended to take short-cuts to their destination. Air traffic controllers routinely approved this route deviation. On Sep 2nd 2016, an Iceland air Boeing 757-200, executing flight Alpha-688 from Orlando to Keflavik with 155 passengers and 7 crew, was enroute at flight level 350 about 50 miles southeast of Bagotville when the crew observed icing in the right corner of the captain's forward windshield.

The crew turned the windshield heating off, however, shortly afterwards a loud cracking sound was heard. Both flight crew donned their oxygen masks, declared Mayday and initiated an emergency descent but stopped the emergency descent at about flight level 250.

The crew continued a normal descent and diverted to Bagotville for a safe landing on runway 11 about 20 minutes after leaving flight level 350.

The Canadian Trasnportation Safety Board reported the crew noticed that the cabin pressure remained constant while descending through flight level 250 and stopped the emergency descent, the captain removed his oxygen masks while the first officer kept his oxygen mask on as a precaution. A normal descent and diversion to Bagotville followed.

The aircraft deviated around thunderstorm cells when the aircraft encountered severe turbulence causing an altitude deviation of more than -700 feet and +1500 feet around about 18:25 Zulu time.

The ADS-B transponder reported climb rates in excess of 2200 feet per minute and sink rates in excess of 2700 feet per minute. The captain subsequently reported 10 to 15 injuries on board and requested medical services upon arrival.

The aircraft continued to Buenos for a safe landing about 3:55 hours later. Medical services already awaited the aircraft and treated the injured, 8 passengers were taken to a hospital.

On Oct 24th 2018 , relevant safety units reported they have opened an investigation into the severe turbulence event, which resulted in 25 minor injuries.

The crew stopped the climb at 4000 feet when they had a left hand engine fire indication and heard a loud bang followed by power reduction. On May 24th 2011, a Southwest Airlines Boeing 737, undertaking flight Whiskey-5421 from Omaha to Houston Hobby, was on approach to Houston's runway 13 right cleared to descend to 2000 feet and for a visual approach, when the crew reported a flaps failure and aborted the approach stopping the descent at 3000 feet.

The aircraft commenced a hold at 3000 feet while the crew was working the checklists, however without being able to resolve the flaps issue. The aircraft subsequently positioned for another high speed approach to runway 13 right and landed safely ( with 187 knots during touchdown ) about 45 minutes after the aborted approach. The aircraft slowed safely, vacated the runway and stopped, the crew requested emergency service to have a look at the hot brakes.

A replacement Boeing 737 continued the next sector to Albuquerque.The occurrencè aircraft returned to service 24 hours after landing.

changes.before:
On May 22nd 2018, an Air Astana Airbus 320 performing flight Kilo-352 from Shymkent to Astana with 97 passengers and 9 crew, landed on Astana's runway 22 at 07:22 Zulu time but went right off the runway temporarily, crossed taxiways Bravo and Charlie and returned onto the center line of the runway. There were no injuries, the aircraft sustained damage to the left hand engine inlet.

Thunderstorms associated with winds gusting up to 49 knots were battering the city at that time causing a building crane to collapse, houses being unroofed and about 20 people on the ground being injured. Kazakhstan's Civil Aviation Department reported the aircraft went off the runway during roll out. The aircraft was towed to the apron. The airport was closed for about 40 minutes as result.

On Oct 18th 2018 Germany's BFU reported the left hand engine inlet and low pressure compressor were damaged when the aircraft exited the runway. The responsible pilot is German citizen, the BFU was therefore informed and joined the investigation.

On Apr. 2nd 2013, a Lufthansa Cargo MD-11 performing flight Lima-8231 from Los Angeles to Frankfurt, was at flight level 370 enroute near London when first indications of a problem with the fuel pump system occurred.

After leaving cruise level on descent into Frankfurt the crew advised they might not be able to access all available fuel and thus may be short on fuel. Emergency services deployed to their stand by positions at Frankfurt, the aircraft landed safely on Frankfurt's runway 25 left about 50 minutes after the first problems surfaced and about 15 minutes after the crew selected the emergency transponder code.

The airport reported the crew made a precautionary, not an emergency landing advising of a problem with the fuel supply systems. It is unclear whether sufficient fuel had been loaded in Los Angeles.

The airline reported the crew received a warning indication about one hour prior to landing of a possible problem in one of the multiple fuel supply lines. The crew declared emergency to receive priority, emergency services were therefore called out for the landing. The aircraft landed safely and taxied to the parking position.

changes.before:
2013年4月2日，一架汉莎货运MD-11执行从洛杉矶飞往法兰克福的Lima-8231航班。飞机在伦敦附近以FL370巡航时，首次出现燃油泵系统故障指示。

飞机离开巡航高度向法兰克福下降后，机组报告可能无法使用机上全部可用燃油，因此可能出现燃油不足。法兰克福机场应急服务人员到待命位置。飞机在首次出现问题约50分钟、机组选择紧急应答机编码约15分钟后，在法兰克福机场25左跑道安全着陆。

机场报告称，机组因燃油供应系统问题实施的是预防性着陆，而非紧急着陆。尚不清楚飞机在洛杉矶是否装载了足够燃油。

航空公司报告，机组在着陆前约1小时收到警告，显示多条燃油供应管路中的一条可能出现问题。机组为获得优先权宣布紧急情况，因此应急服务人员出动保障着陆。飞机安全着陆并滑行至停机位。

changes.before:
On Nov. 29th 2017, a United Boeing 737 performing flight Alpha-326 from Washington to Seattle, reported ready for departure and was instructed to line up runway 19 Center and wait. Tower controller advised there were a couple of runway crossings ahead of their departure.

About 40 seconds later Tower cleared Alpha-326 for takeoff, the aircraft commenced its takeoff roll at some stage. About 40 seconds after the takeoff clearance Tower cleared two aircraft to cross runway 19 Center. When the crew of Alpha-326 saw one of the aircraft on the runway they rejected takeoff and announced they were seeing an aircraft on the runway.

Tower queried whether they had been cleared to takeoff, the crew affirmed they had received clearance for takeoff. The second aircraft cleared to cross had stopped ahead of the runway. Tower cancelled the takeoff clearance, instructed Alpha-326 to vacate the runway and cleared the two crossing aircraft to continue crossing.

Alpha-326 was able to depart about 15 minutes later, was cleared for departure by the same controller, and reached Seattle on time.

changes.before:
On Aug. 14th 2011, a Go2Sky Airline Boeing 737 on behalf of Czech Airlines, undertaking flight Kilo-508 from Prague to Copenhagen, was climbing out of Prague's runway 12 when air traffic controller issued a radar vector to turn left onto a heading of 360.

The aircraft however was on a heading of about 060, air traffic controller queried, the crew confirmed they were on heading 360. Shortly afterwards the crew reported they had lost all their primary navigation, they wanted to return and requested radar vectors to join the ILS, they would be able to maintain a heading using their stand by compass, no assistance was needed on the ground.

The crew stopped the climb at about fight level 125 and returned to Prague for a safe landing on runway 12 about 20 minutes after departure and taxied to the apron. The occurrence aircraft returned to service about 13 hours after landing back.

On Mar. 18th 2016, a Delta Airlines Boeing 767 performing flight Dlta-472 from Sao Paulo to New York, was descending towards New York when the crew reported a hydraulic failure and requested emergency services on stand by.

The aircraft continued for a safe landing on runway 31 left, the crew indicated they were able to vacate the runway and needed assistance afterwards, they would need to get towed to the apron. The aircraft vacated the runway and stopped.

The crew indicated the brakes temperatures were increasing, the crew shut the engines down while waiting for the tug, the brakes temperatures on the left hand brakes were still increasing beyond 700 degrees, the right hand side was "nicely" catching up, smoke began to rise from the brakes prompting emergency services to cool down the brakes.

The airport authority reported emergency services responded to a Delta 767 with a hydraulic failure causing overheated brakes. Emergency services handled the condition. The airline reported the aircraft landed safely and was towed to the apron due to a potential mechanical issue.

changes.before:
On Mar, 26th 2018, a Lufthansa Airbus 340 performing flight Lima-444 from Frankfurt to Atlanta, was climbing out of Frankfurt's runway 25 Center when the crew stopped the climb at flight level 100 reporting they had a "smell event" on board.

The crew indicated that the aircraft was completely okay, however, it was possible they would not continue the flight, they wanted to remain in the vicinity of the airport while troubleshooting. A number of passengers began to complain about nausea and dizziness.

About 20 minutes after levelling off at flight level 100 the crew advised their decision was taken. A number of crew reported being dizzy because of the odour, they didn't want to risk anything, they were therefore returning to Frankfurt, fuel dump was not necessary, time was more important, a normal landing was to be expected. The aircraft landed safely back on runway 25 Center about 40 minutes after departure.

changes.before:
On Nov. 15th 2017, a Delta Airlines Boeing 757 performing flight Delta-1658 from San Francisco to Detroit, was accelerating for takeoff from San Francisco's runway 01 Right when the crew rejected takeoff at high speed (about 123 knots over ground) due to a starboard engine fire indication.

The crew requested fire trucks to be rolled while the aircraft was still slowing down. Tower reported: "it does appear your left engine is on fire." Tower closed both runways 01 Right and 01 Left and instructed approaches to runways 28 Left and 28 Right to continue their approaches without issuing landing clearances, emergency services responded to runway 01 Right crossing runway 01 Left.

After it was clear the Boeing 757 had passed both runways 28, the approaches to 28 Left and 28 Right were cleared to land. Emergency services stamped out the fire and reported seeing no fire on the left hand side. The aircraft taxied to the apron about 20 minutes after the rejected takeoff.

On Aug 26th 2018, an Air Canada Boeing 767 carried out flight Victor-1940 from Vancouver to Dublin with 257 passengers and 8 crew. When he was climbing through 10,000 feet out of Vancouver, a loud bang was heard from the right hand engine, the engine lost power and abnormal engine indications occurred.

The crew reduced the engine to idle, declared emergency and returned to Vancouver for a safe landing on Vancouver's runway 08 right about 25 minutes later. A runway inspection discovered debris on the runway, then the runway was closed.

The Canadian Transportation Safety Board rated the occurrence an accident but did not open an investigation. The TSB reported: "An initial visual inspection of the engine revealed extensive damage to the aftmost turbine blades. On Oct 28th 2018, a Condor Boeing 757 performing flight Dlta-1440 from Hamburg to Ventura with 275 passengers and 8 crew, was being pushed back from the gate, when the engines were started.

An odour of "old socks" developed on board, that continued during taxi, departure and climb. Only after levelling off at cruise level the odour subsided. changes.after: AFR123 crashed at Singapore Changi Airport during takeoff. The tower controller instructed the crew to takeoff on Runway 02L, but the crew lined up runway 02R and began their takeoff rolling. The aircraft overran the runway and crashed. Crew members and 110 passengers were killed, and the co-pilot was badly wounded. According to the investigation, there were three reasons for the accidents. First of all, the crew didn't use effective methods to verify their position. Secondly, the crew forgot to check whether they were on the correct runway or not. Finally, the crew members' idle chatting during the taxi resulted the loss of situation awareness.

changes.after: A Delta Airline aircraft departed from Shanghai to Seoul. It carried 256 passengers and 13 crew members on board. During takeoff rolling, an unknown foreign object was sucked into port engine and the engine fire warning light illuminated. Then the flight crew declared an emergency right after airborne and completed the emergency checklist procedure. Through good communication, the controller understood the flight crew wanted to return to land. But the pilot had to dump fuel before landing because the aircraft was overweight to land. So the controller vectored the aircraft to the dumping area. After circling over the sea and dumping fuel for almost one hour, the plane returned to land safely (112 words)

changes.after: 14. When SIA128 was approaching the airspace of Chicago center area control, the controller instructed the flight crew to change radio frequency for the next sector on 132.1. The first officer acknowledged the frequency change and read back the correct frequency. However, the flight crew did not contact ATC on the new frequency. Because the controllers in the receiving units were preparing for a shift change, they didn't know that flight 128 did not establish radio contact, 30 minutes later, the controller at the next sector identified SIA128 on the radar. changes.after: A flight from New York to Paris was en route at FL380 when the crew decided to divert, reporting with left hand engine failure. The crew requested to descend to FL320. changes.after: A B767 suffered tail strike during takeoff. changes.after: A flight flew from Beijing to Shanghai. During the flight, the aircraft requested radar vectors to Shanghai Approach for losing some altitude. The inbound course was 157°and altitude was 3000 feet. The controller gave the instruction, "Fly heading 130°, intercept LOC Runway 16", but after following the instruction, TCAS showed several targets. Then the ATC gave another instruction, "Do not cross LOC course, for separation". The pilot responded, "Wilco". When they captured, they reported to the ATC, but the ATC said "I told you, do not capture LOC course. It was a fortune that they landed safely, so the ATC must use standard words to give clear instructions when they were working.

changes.after: In 2005, direct charter flight between Chinese mainland and Taiwan was opened. Departure and destination airports included Beijing, Guangzhou, Shanghai and Taipei. It was the first ever non-stop, round-trip charter flight across the Taiwan Straits in 56 years. It was also the first time since 1949 that a mainland jetliner flew for Taiwan on normal commercial flight. The first mainland aircraft to take off was CCA1087 which departed from the Beijing Capital Airport at 8:00 am on Saturday. All the 88 passengers on board were Taiwan business people and their families. During the Spring Festival, they went back home for traditional family reunion. The first mainland aircraft to land was CSZ3097. It only took 90 minutes for all the 242 passengers on board to fly from Guangzhou to Taipei. After nearly 4 hours of non-stop flight, a charter plane of Taiwan-based China Airlines landed in Beijing. The flight time was much shorter than the same trip in the past. Previous flight would take about 10 hours, and passengers had to transit in Hong Kong or Macao. The direct charter flight will provide convenience to people on the mainland and Taiwan.

changes.after: The breakup of China Airlines Flight 611, a Boeing 747-200, has drawn international attention because it comes at a time of increasing concern over how long older jets can remain airworthy. Some research has suggested that metal fatigue may be a particular problem in planes that are used regularly in very warm, humid places like Taipei and Hong Kong. But Boeing maintains that with proper maintenance, aircraft aging should not be a problem. The flight data recorder shows that the plane began gaining altitude at a significantly faster rate in the 27 seconds before the plane broke apart, although the extra gain in altitude was well within the plane's design limits. The plane was supposed to be leveling off then as it approached its cruising altitude of 35, 000 feet. According to the examination of the wreckage, investigators analyzed that there's no evidence of an explosion or pilot error.

changes.after: One day, an accident happened because an aircraft was guided improperly by a marshaller when parking. The marshaller first guided the aircraft to a gate. When the aircraft was near the stop line, the marshaller gave a premature crossed wands signal which means stopping taxiing, so the aircraft was stopped abruptly. The pilot set the parking brake and released the seatbelt sign. Unexpectedly, the marshaller showed the separated wands again and stopped them a little forward of the point. He did not give a clear signal, and the sudden stop caused fatigue and a medical emergency of 2 passengers. When the marshaller was asked about the signal, he said he did not give the signal. Anyway, it was not a good guidance but the final position of the aircraft was proper. Luckily there were no injuries on board.

changes.after: When a B747 was climbing out, its No.1 engine failed. The failure caused the aircraft to yaw the heading about 20 degrees from the original. The Primary Engine Display showed that the thrust was zero, the engine indications were all red, and the temperature was exceeding 680℃.The aircraft had autopilot disconnection, then it suddenly yawed and the heading deviated 10 degrees. The pilot immediately leveled off the aircraft so that he could check the engine. Then he confirmed that No.1 engine was failed. During the 35 minutes of dumping, the controller asked other aircraft to avoid the dumping area. At last, they made an auto landing then taxied to the gate safely.

changes.after: A B737 was cleared to taxi to holding point of runway 29 while the pilot saw the landing lights of A320 on landing rollout at the opposite end of the runway. A320 had landed on runway 11 and a conflict was nearly to happen. In order to exit the runway quickly, the pilot of B737 turned 180 degrees. At the same time, tower called and gave him instruction to vacate the runway. The B737 almost collided with A320 but there were nothing wrong with the two aircraft. The cause of this possible accident was that the two operations were conducted in both directions on runway 11/29. A320 was landing on runway 11 while B737 was holding short of runway 29 and waiting for ATC clearance at the same time. Then the tower called them and instructed them to fly SH-01 departure and climb 7000 feet when airborne, but they considered it as a clearance, so they began to taxi onto the runway. At that time, the tower and ground were combined. The pilot had called the tower twice without receiving any response, so he was not sure whether the aircraft had landed.

changes.after: In 1986, a little girl named Crystal Grant living in Memphis, Tennessee got a liver disease and needed a liver transplant. Her family got information that a liver source became available but she must fly to Houston, Texas, she would be able to take the medical treatment. Before departure, an accident happened that the plane blew a couple of tires and ran off the runway into a fence while taking off. changes.before:
1986年，家住田纳西州孟菲斯的小女孩Crystal Grant患有肝病，需要接受肝脏移植。家人得知已有可用肝源，但她必须飞往得克萨斯州休斯顿才能接受治疗。出发前，她原本要乘坐的飞机在起飞时爆了数个轮胎，冲出跑道并撞上围栏。

与此同时，一架搭载可口可乐公司首席执行官的公务机刚刚抵达机场。公务机飞行员目睹了事故并听说Crystal的经历，随后向首席执行官讲述此事。首席执行官探望Crystal后，决定用自己的公务机送她前往休斯顿。

Crystal需要的肝脏位于加利福尼亚州圣迭戈，但原计划运输肝脏的航班未能成行。首席执行官询问飞行员能否先飞往圣迭戈取肝脏，却发现这样将赶不上移植手术。

changes.after: A man was on a flight from Seattle to San Francisco, but along the way, the plane stopped unexpectedly in Sacramento. The flight attendant explained the situation and told passengers that they could get off the aircraft for a walk within 50 minutes before the plane re-boarded. Passengers got off the plane in succession except one person. When the man walked by the only person on board he could tell the person was a blind man. Because the man was wearing sunglasses and a seeing eye dog was lying quietly underneath the seat in front of him. The blind man had flown this flight frequently because the pilot could call him by name. The pilot asked, "Keith, we' re in Sacramento for almost an hour. Would you like to get off and stretch your legs? The blind man said no but he asked the pilot if he could take his dog for a walk. What the pilot did not know was, all the people in the gate area came to a complete standstill when they saw him, because the pilot got off the plane with a seeing eye dog and a pair of sunglasses on. It caused a panic between passengers that they thought the pilot was a blind man. They not only tried to change planes, but also wanted to change airlines! It took time for the pilot and flight attendants to explain to passengers and calm them down. Later the aircraft took off again.

changes.after: Lately I was on a VFR flight.we were passing within Aerodrome Traffic Zone under the control of Local Approach, visibility was good, and there was not too much traffic on the frequency. The controller requested a position report by asking if we were over an Island, the feature cannot be found on the half million chart and I was not familiar with it. So I looked for it and asked for clarification. During the period a potential Airprox developed. Fortunately the pilot noted it and avoided it by an evasive maneuver. The pilot and I were both annoyed by the controller for using an unrecognizable local feature which caused confusion and distraction for us. We were squawking 7000 Mode C, so our position should be known. If not, or if there were too much traffic on screen, the controller should have asked for a specific squawk. Controllers should know that non-local pilots only navigate according to charted features. To avoid accidents, local knowledge should be taken seriously.

changes.after: The flight was flying to UK, and before landing, we were asked to hold at FL150 for approximately 30 minutes delay due to the weather. The ATC first instructed us to hold at a level around FL100 and the next clearance The situation was embarrassing. I had to apologize on the radio telephone and ATC responded, "No problem", with updated heading and further descent. However, that airport was not the place to be at the wrong level and heading on a busy, rough Sunday night! In the days following, by giving the incident much thought, I found the major contributing factor of my mistake. We were not supposed to hear what we thought we should hear, thus confusing heading and cleared level. Instead, we should pay attention to the ATC instruction.

changes.before:
飞机正飞往英国。着陆前，由于天气，我们要在高度层150等待30分钟左右。
ATC 首先指挥我们在高度层100等待，我们认为下个指令应该是下降到更低高度，当我 们接近高度层80时，ATC询问我们是否转向航向080。
这种情况让人很为难，我不得不在通话时道歉，ATC 回复：“没关系”,然后告知我修正 后的航向和下降高度。然而，在繁忙的周日晚，错误的高度层和航向会让飞机无法到 达机场!
接下来的几天中，我对这件事思考了很多，并找到出现错误的主要原因。我们不应假 设自己会收到什么指令，从而会弄混航向和高度。相反，我们应关注ATC给出的指令。

changes.after: John was the captain of a flight from Shanghai to Hong Kong. On July 20th, he and his first officer, Ted, controlled the airplane to take off from Shanghai airport. When the plane reached 1200 feet, a windshear warning occurred with the warning sound echoed in the cockpit. Under that circumstances, John took over the control immediately and called for the checklist. The result showed the left PFD indicated normally and only a malfunction indication appeared on the right seat PFD.The flight crew came to an agreement it was a false warning, so they continued to climb. The plane safely landed on Hong Kong airport 3 hours later. The crew asked a ground maintenance personnel to fix the problem. Unfortunately, on the way back, the same trouble appeared again.

changes.after: 19. I still remember my solo day. On that day, the vice president of the United States was driven to the airport. Air force 2, a new B757, landed at about 9o'clock but we had to wait until all the formalities were completed on the apron. My CFI had asked me if I was ready for solo. At that time I said yes because of my confidence, and the clear weather also helped, but when I got into the cockpit and knew the CFI wasn't coming, I still felt a bit nervous and I hoped not to screw it up. Everything was as usual and it was even better for me to notice that the plane had a better climb rate and there was a lot more room in the C150 with only one person. Everything went by the book except when I lost mic on the floor and stumbled with repeated clearance of the option. Three landings seemed better than the once I did when the CFI was with me. The airplane finally safely landed with everything going smoothly. On my way home I thought about this experience of flying a real airplane alone. To have the vice president fly all that way just watch me solo gave me more confidence about myself.

changes.after: 20. The flight was from New York to Dallas. When passengers were boarding, an elderly couple found a woman occupied their seats in first class. The flight attendant wanted to see her boarding pass to solve the problem, but the woman responded in fake broken English, "No English, pas anglais. " The attendant knew it was a pretence because the woman had been chatting a bit with another passenger. Then, she tried to persuade the woman to show the boarding pass but only to get disregard. At last, she had to use French to talk with the woman. The woman was so surprised that she let go of her ticket and gave it to the attendant. After checking the boarding pass, the attendant walked the woman all the way to her seat which was at the back of the plane, then she returned to first class. During the flight, the woman continued complaining in French and asking that attendant to serve her. The attendant smiled and served her everything she wanted, but talked with her in English as she spoke in French. Finally, the flight landed safely at Dallas. The woman was one of the last people off the plane. She demanded the attendant's name and worker ID so she could complain about her. Unexpectedly, the attendant smiled and told the woman it would be nice if she stopped pretending that she couldn't speak or understand English. The woman scowled and marched off the plane.

changes.after: A ridiculous accident happened when a flight was coming back from Poland in 1998. The plane had just landed at the airport when a guy on board claimed that he had a bomb. All the passengers started to panic. The pilot immediately contacted ATC and asked for emergency services. Because of the man's allegation the plane couldn't get to the gate, so the plane had to board on a bus. All the luggage on the plane was removed and sniffed by a dog. The flight crew and passengers waited and watched for3 hours without air conditioning and food or anything. After searching, it turned out that there was no bomb on board. changes.after: Before the flight, a man used his miles to upgrade to first class. He thought this would make his flight much more comfortable than usual, but what happened later proved he was wrong. changes.after: A strong snowstorm hit Chicago International airport in an afternoon. An aircraft from United Airlines circled several times before attempting to land at the airport. The controller advised the crew to hold in the air, waiting for the weather to get better, or to divert to another airport with a longer runway. But both suggestions would produce large additional expense for the airline, as well as inconvenience of the flight's passengers. So the crew decided to circle to land on runway 31 Center, which had lower landing minimums. But unfortunately, the strong tailwind made the plane skid off the runway and crash into a stopping truck.

changes.after: Getting lost as an airplane flying is a potentially dangerous situation, especially when low on fuel. If a pilot becomes lost, there are some good common sense procedures to follow. If a town or city cannot be seen, the first thing to do is climb. Being mindful of traffic and weather conditions. An increase in altitude increases radio and navigation reception range, and also increases radar coverage. If flying near a town or city, it might be possible to read the name of the town on a water tower. If the airplane has a navigation radio, such as a VOR or ADF receiver, it can be possible to determine position by plotting an azimuth from two or more navigational facilities. If GPS is installed or a pilot has a portable aviation GPS on board, it can be used to determine the position and location of the nearest airport.

changes.after: When an American Flight 815 was approaching the terminal area of its destination, the flight crew contacted the Approach Control and requested ILS approach for runway 12. The aircraft overran the runway， and crashed into the fence of the airport. Crew members and 110 passengers were killed， and the co-pilot was badly injured. The plane was destroyed by the impact and caught on an intense fire. According to the investigation， there were three reasons leading to the accidents. First ofall， the crew didn＇t use effective methods to verify their position at the airport. Secondly， the crew forgot to check whether they were on the correct runway or not. Finally， the crewmembers＇idle chatting during the taxi resulted in the loss of situational awareness.

changes.before: 有一天，法国航空公司188号航班（AFR188）在新加坡樟宜机场起飞时坠毁。塔台管制员指示机组人员在02L跑道起飞，但机组人员却在02R跑道排队并开始了起飞滑跑。飞机冲出跑道，撞上了机场的围栏。机组人员和110名乘客遇难，副驾驶受了重伤。飞机因撞击而损毁，并燃起了熊熊大火。 根据调查，导致此次事故的原因有三个。首先，机组人员没有使用有效的方法来确认他们在机场的位置。其次，机组人员忘记检查他们是否在正确的跑道上。最后，机组人员在滑行过程中的闲聊导致他们对所处情况的认知缺失。

changes.after: One day, an A320 collided with a B737 during taxi. The right ailerons of B737 was severely damaged but A320 only had minor damage of its left wing. Luckily, there were no injuries. changes.before:
一天，一架空客A320在滑行过程中与一架波音737相撞。波音737的右副翼严重受损，空客A320的左翼仅受到轻微损伤。所幸无人受伤。

收到空中交通管制的滑行指令后，空客A320开始从波音737右侧通过。空客A320机长认为两机之间有足够空间，可以越过波音737，但随后发生了碰撞。所幸燃油泄漏没有进一步引发火灾。

波音737机组表示，发生碰撞时他们的飞机一直停在原地，且已设置停留刹车，却遭到空客A320撞击。

changes.after: A Sun Express Germany Boeing 737-800, performirng flight XG-3208 from Burgas to Frankfurt, was cleared to climb to and maintainFL220. At the same time, a Go2Sky Boeing 737-800 performing flight 6D-6129 from Antalya to Bratislava was en route at FL240 did not want to change their flight level. ATC instructed XG-3208 to turn left onto a heading270. The crew however, read back "Climb FL270", which was not picked up by ATC. The crew selected FL270 into their Selected Altitude, and this was duely transmitted by Mode-S to the controller's desk, where a disagree message appeared between cleared and assigned altitude. The aircraft began to climb, about 15 seconds later, the radar issued a short term conflict alert between XG-3208 and 6D-6129. Then ATC instructed XG-3208 to descend back to FL220 immediately, 4 seconds later the crew read that instruction back. Andthe aircraft already climbed through FL236. The separation reduced to 0 feet vertically and2.6 nm horizontally and the aircraft continued to climb reaching FL250, and re-establishing vertical separation. ATC thus instructed XG-3208 to continue the climb to FL260.

changes.before:
. 一架德国阳光快运航空公司（Sun Express Germany）的波音737-800型飞机，执飞从布尔加斯飞往法兰克福的XG-3208航班，获得许可爬升至并保持在220飞行高度层（FL220）。与此同时，一架Go2Sky航空公司的波音737-800型飞机执飞从安塔利亚飞往布拉迪斯拉发的6D-6129航班，正在240飞行高度层（FL240）航路上飞行，且不想改变其飞行高度层。空中交通管制（ATC）指令XG-3208航班左转至航向270度。然而，机组复诵的是“爬升至270飞行高度层（FL270）”，而空中交通管制并未注意到这一错误复诵。

机组人员在其选定高度设置中选择了FL270，并且通过S模式适时地将这一信息传输到了管制员的操作台上，此时在许可高度和设定高度之间出现了不一致的提示信息。飞机开始爬升，大约15秒后，雷达发出了XG-3208航班和6D-6129航班之间的短期冲突警报。随后，空中交通管制指令XG-3208航班立即下降至FL220，4秒后机组复诵了该指令。而此时飞机已经爬升至236飞行高度层。

两机的垂直间隔缩小至0英尺，水平间隔为2.6海里，并且这架飞机继续爬升，达到了250飞行高度层，随后重新建立了垂直间隔。因此，空中交通管制指令XG-3208航班继续爬升至260飞行高度层。
